plan.summary: This 4-week block is the first step of a 12-week off-camp boxing plan. With only one 60-minute S&C session each week and bodyweight-only equipment, the goal is to build basic lower-body and full-body power, simple strength endurance, trunk strength, and a small conditioning base without creating too much fatigue for boxing practice. Week 1 is used to establish a simple bodyweight performance baseline rather than barbell training maxes, and the main progression starts in Week 2.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build basic force, power, trunk strength, and repeat-effort conditioning with simple bodyweight work that is easy to recover from.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the same movement patterns with harder variations, tighter execution, and slightly denser conditioning.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength qualities while shifting more emphasis toward faster, sharper explosive work and fresher output.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can on every rep. Land softly and reset between reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the countermovement jump feels uncoordinated. Start from a still quarter squat and jump fast.

exercises.name: Push-Up Test Set
exercises.reps: Max clean reps stopping one rep before form breaks
exercises.notes: This is your Week 1 upper-body baseline. Use strict reps, full body tension, and stop before your hips sag or your head reaches first.

performanceTarget.prompt: Log your best clean set so we can track your bodyweight strength endurance over time.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up Test Set
substitutionOptions.notes: Use hands on a bench, table, or sturdy box if floor push-ups are too hard. Keep the body in one straight line.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Control the way down, keep your front foot flat, and drive up smoothly. Use bodyweight only and leave 2 reps in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if split squats bother the knees or if space is limited. Step back under control and stand up tall.

exercises.name: 1a. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use a variation you can do cleanly. Stop with 1-2 reps in reserve and keep each rep crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a higher hand position to keep reps clean and controlled.

substitutionOptions.name: Knee Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if you cannot hold good body alignment on standard reps.

exercises.name: 1b. Prone Back Extension Hold
exercises.notes: Lift the chest lightly off the floor, squeeze the glutes, and keep the neck long. Do not crank the low back.

substitutionOptions.name: Superman Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Lift arms and legs slightly only if you can keep the low back comfortable.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Keep the ribs down and low back gently pressed toward the floor. Shorten the lever if you lose position.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the hollow hold is too difficult. Move slowly and keep the trunk locked in.

exercises.name: Mountain Climber Intervals
exercises.notes: Move fast but stay controlled. Keep shoulders stacked over hands and hips level throughout.

substitutionOptions.name: High-Knee Run in Place Intervals
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if wrist loading is uncomfortable. Stay light on the feet and pump the arms.

exercises.notes: Jump hard on every rep and fully reset between efforts. Stop if jump height clearly drops.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a simpler jump pattern. Stay stiff through takeoff and land softly.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if split squats feel awkward. Keep the step smooth and stable.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
